newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Weak margins drag down light grades.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Weak margins drag down light grades.

text.p: Asia's light crudes saw limited support in August, while South Korean refiners continue to cover their requirements with West African grades.
A major heard sold a VLCC of August loading Bonny Light to a South Korean refiner at dated Brent +40 cents per barrel.
The trade could not be confirmed, but would be only the second cargo of West African crude ever bought by the refiner.
The refiner bought its first July loading Bonny Light crude in early June.
Another South Korean refiner also heard bought a VLCC of Aug loading Odudu/Djeno from a European major.
Malaysia confirmed selling 450,000 barrels of August Tapis, heard at Tapis APPI +1/+2 cents to a western trader.
But many traders still see limited upside for the light Asian crudes in August, citing weak margins and thin demand.
Reduced output from Cossack and Griffin are not expected to boost prices.
Maintenance works at the Cossack crude field is planned for August, while the production of Griffin field has been cut due to problems at the floating production facility.
But a major holding an early August cargo of Kutubu said found limited interest.
The heavy Asian grades were steady, but cooler temperatures in Japan on Friday kept utilities on the sidelines, reassessing their summer requirements.
Malaysia awarded its first Bunga Kekwa crude tender to a major at Tapis APPI -$1.00. The tender closed on Thursday and received four bids, mainly from refiners.
In the Middle East crude market, August Murban was heard done at ADNOC -27. But traders say at least 1.2 million barrels of Murban and 400,000 barrels of Lower Zakum were still on offer for August.
